checks: A full-dimensional simplex projects to a full-dimensional base set; selecting n+1 independent projected vertices leaves d barycentric coordinates. If their variations and the base variation vanish, the other barycentric variations have zero sum and base moment and therefore vanish.
Using one selected vertex as origin makes the determinant into (z,x) equal n!|Q|. Dividing by the original (n+d)!|C| gives J, and the fixed base block makes J also the fiber Jacobian.

For fixed x the remaining barycentric weights have total 1-S, including S=1. Fubini of the finite fiber indicators gives the exact density version. At n=1 the closed integer count includes both endpoints; n=0 gives one.
The source §1 (1)–(5) has the same scope. Constant J transports the normalized positive-mass law and its centroid by the affine map.

overlap.comparison: It uses the general indicator-sum marginal for coordinate-reflection families; it does not supply the barycentric normal form, Jacobian, or projected-simplex count for ambient simplices.
Its one specified six-dimensional simplex uses the same selected-coordinate idea; it does not establish the general all-n normal form.

readability: The selected versus unselected vertex roles and the positive-mass proviso are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The base-preserving coordinate map, its determinant, and the pointwise lattice-count marginal all follow in the stated full-volume model.
